land.text: Demak (Bintara) on the north coast of Central Java, a vassal of Majapahit 1475-1478

predecessors.note: Infobox 'Vassal state of Majapahit (1475-1478)'; independence 1478 after the collapse of Kertabhumi of Trowulan and the rise of Girindrawardhana of Daha; 'established three years later, in 1481 CE'.

land.text: Pajang under Hadiwijaya (Jaka Tingkir), to whom the Demak regalia passed in 1568

successors.note: Cliopatria's Kingdom of Pajana row (1572-1587) has the same shape as Demak 1519-1551; nothing covers 1569-1571. Demak survived as a vassal of Pajang under Sunan Pangiri.

capitals.name: Bintara (Demak)
capitals.note: Infobox 'Capital: Bintara, Demak'; the regalia moved to Pajang in 1568.

rulers.name: Trenggana
rulers.note: killed in 1546; the page also gives him an earlier reign c. 1505-1518

rulers.name: Arya Penangsang
rulers.note: dethroned by vassals and killed in 1568

keyframe_review.note: 7,452 km2 (25 cells, 62 percent of a 50 km radius round Demak): the capital Bintara and its coast. The page gives no area. Infobox: vassal of Majapahit 1475-1478, independent 1478, 'dominated Semarang, Jepara, Tuban, and Gresik'.

45,552 km2 (175 cells): Central Java (71 percent of the province), Yogyakarta and the Kediri country (88 percent of a 50 km radius), identical to Cliopatria's later Kingdom of Pajana. Kediri (Daha) fell to Demak in 1518, which explains the East Java part; the page does not date the Central Java hinterland. Tuban (c. 1527) is not in the shape and comes from the ledger. 47 percent of this shape also lies inside Cliopatria's Majapahit shape (1500). Unverified beyond the Daha line: page budget.

union.text: Tuban, 'an old Majapahit port', conquered c. 1527

keyframe_review.note: The same 45,552 km2 for 1547-1551 plus Tuban. The page ends the sultanate in 1568 (Arya Penangsang killed, regalia to Pajang), not 1551; Trenggana was killed in 1546 and his son Prawata in 1549.

correction.text: the 1547 shape kept to 1568, when Hadiwijaya took sovereignty and moved the regalia to Pajang

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria's Demak row ends 1551 and its Kingdom of Pajana starts 1572. The page has Penangsang on the throne 1549-1568 and Hadiwijaya only an adipati of Pajang until then (the infobox lists a Pajang entry '1549-1582', which conflicts with the 1568 body text); the shape is held unchanged and its reality is unverified.

region.text: Bintara (Demak) on the north coast of Central Java

ledger.note: 1475: Raden Patah's Demak appears as a vassal of Majapahit. Infobox 'Vassal state of Majapahit (1475-1478)' and 'Raden Patah (r. 1475-1518)'; independence 1478, the kingdom 'established three years later, in 1481 CE'.

region.text: Daha (the Kediri country), where Demak defeated Patih Udara in 1518

ledger.note: 1518: Demak defeats Daha. 'Demak fought Patih Udara of Daha. The land army went through Madiun, and the fleet under Pati Unus sailed via Sedayu. Daha was defeated in 1518'; Raden Patah died that year.

region.text: the Central Java hinterland of Cliopatria's 1519 shape (Semarang, Jepara and the Mataram country)

ledger.note: 1518: Cliopatria's 1519 shape is six times the 1475 core; the page says Demak 'dominated Semarang, Jepara, Tuban, and Gresik' and that Trenggana 'took the remnants of Majapahit' (no year). Year and extent are bridged from the shape.

region.text: Palembang: 'Raden Patah gained control of Jambi and Palembang in eastern Sumatra'

ledger.note: By 1518: Palembang under Demak's control. The page gives the control within Raden Patah's reign (1475-1518) and no year; the Palembang page says a Demak nobleman, Geding Suro, fled to Palembang after Demak's fall and 'established a new dynasty'.
By 1518: Jambi under Demak's control; same undated page line as Palembang.

region.text: Banten and Sunda Kalapa, taken from the Kingdom of Sunda by Fatahillah

ledger.note: 1527: Fatahillah storms Sunda Kalapa. 'Fatahillah was ordered to take Banten and Sunda Kelapa (later Jayakarta) from the Kingdom of Sunda, after the 1522 Portuguese-Sunda alliance'; the Cirebon-Demak force took the harbour 'just before the Portuguese returned' (Sunda Kingdom page). Banten became a vassal sultanate, a province of Cirebon on the Banten page.
c. 1527: Demak conquers Tuban. 'Tuban, an old Majapahit port, was conquered' (the page's 'c. 1527').

1531: peace with Sunda. 'a peace treaty was concluded between King Surawisesa of Sunda and' Cirebon; the Banten page says Surawisesa signed with Demak and Cirebon and that Old Banten became a province under Cirebon (see the Cirebon dossier's vassal event). The zone does not become Demak's direct land.

1546: Trenggana killed at Pasuruan; Demak's reach over Sumatra is not recorded after this. The page is silent on when its control of Palembang ended; the Palembang page has Geding Suro fleeing there after Demak's fall.
1546: as for Palembang; the page is silent.

1568: Arya Penangsang is killed and the sultanate ends. 'After Penangsang's death in 1568, Hadiwijaya took sovereignty and moved Demak's regalia and sacred objects to Pajang'; Pajang became the suzerain and Demak its vassal under Sunan Pangiri.

wars.name: Demak war on Daha
wars.outcome: Patih Udara's Daha defeated in 1518; Raden Patah died soon after.
wars.note: Land army by Madiun, fleet under Pati Unus by Sedayu.

wars.name: Demak expeditions against Portuguese Malacca
wars.outcome: Both failed. The Demak page puts Pati Unus's first fleet (about 100 ships) in 1513 and the second (375 ships) in 1521, when he died; the Portuguese Malacca page has Demak sending ships in 1511 and a second campaign in 1521 'which also failed and cost the Demak ruler his life'.
wars.note: Pages disagree on the first year (1511 or 1513).

wars.name: Cirebon-Demak conquest of Sunda Kalapa and Banten
wars.outcome: Sunda Kalapa renamed Jayakarta; Banten under Hasanuddin as a province of Cirebon; peace with King Surawisesa in 1531.
wars.note: Joint with Cirebon (see sultanate-of-cirebon); the Banten page says Demak and Cirebon also beat a Portuguese fleet in 1527.

wars.name: Trenggana's Pasuruan campaign
wars.outcome: Ended with Trenggana's death in 1546; no land changed hands.
wars.note: The page says Surabaya appears as the home of the duke who killed Trenggana.

certainty.note: A coastal sultanate whose reach is a list of ports and principalities; no treaty line is dated by the pages opened.

sources.title: Demak Sultanate
sources.note: Identity, rulers, Daha 1518, Tuban c. 1527, Sunda Kalapa 1527, Malacca expeditions, dissolution 1568; no area.

sources.title: Sunda Kingdom
sources.note: Cirebon-Demak conquest of Sunda Kalapa 1527 and the 1531 treaty.

sources.title: Banten Sultanate
sources.note: Banten a province of Cirebon after 1526; 1531 treaty with Demak and Cirebon.

notes:
Cliopatria row 'Demak Sultanate' 1475-1551: shapes reviewed ok / adjust; the row ends 17 years before the page's end (1568, Penangsang killed, regalia to Pajang) and the Kingdom of Pajana row begins in 1572, so 1552-1568 is covered by a new keyframe that repeats the 1547 shape. The sultanate was a vassal of Majapahit 1475-1478 (infobox): that tint is the Majapahit dossier's. The 1519 shape equals Cliopatria's Pajana 1572 shape exactly (175 cells).
Not settled: how much of Central Java and the south coast Demak held after 1518 (the page lists Semarang, Jepara, Tuban and Gresik as dominated and says Trenggana took Majapahit's remnants without a year); the control of Palembang and Jambi (the page gives it to Raden Patah without a year; vassal events at confidence 1, bridging); whether Banten was Demak's or Cirebon's vassal (Demak page: 'Banten later became a vassal sultanate'; Banten page: de jure province of Cirebon 1526-1552).
Disagreements: first Malacca expedition 1511 (Portuguese Malacca page) or 1513 (Demak page); Banten taken 1526 (Banten infobox) or 1527 (Demak page); the infobox's Pajang entry (1549-1582) against the 1568 body text; Demak founding 1475 (reign), 1478 (independence) or 1481 (kingdom established).
Counterparts needing dossiers: Jambi before the sultanate; Pasuruan (Hindu principality, 1546); Daha is not a Cliopatria row (Majapahit's Cliopatria row ends 1518).
Page budget: Demak page plus three pages shared with the Cirebon and Malacca dossiers.
